title: Egg Foo Young Gravy
description: A light brown roux and a little sesame oil make this Chinese-American egg foo young gravy silky enough to ladle over soft eggs.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: unsalted dry drinking sherry
ingredients.note: Use drinking sherry, without added salt.

steps.title: Toast the roux
steps.text: Stir {oil} and {fl} in the skillet over medium-low heat for 3 minutes until light tan and fragrant.

steps.title: Whisk in the broth
steps.text: Pour {ch} into the roux in a thin stream, whisking constantly until lump-free.

steps.title: Simmer the gravy
steps.text: Whisk in {a}, {sh} and {wp}. Simmer gently for 4–5 minutes until the gravy coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Ladle over soft eggs or a bowl of rice and serve the extra gravy warm alongside.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, omit white pepper and use water instead of sherry. Nutrition counts the full sherry before simmering. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 46 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 3.4 g total carbohydrate, 2.9 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 99 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 42 kcal, 0.7 g protein, 2.4 g total carbohydrate, 2.9 g fat, 0.1 g fiber, 32 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.

steps.title: Set up the cooking vessel
steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
